props.gloss_en: Shmuel: 'and they anoint themselves with the chief of oils' (Amos 6:6) -- this is palyaton
R' Yehuda ben Bava decreed even on palyaton
and they did not agree with him
'who drink in mizrekei of wine' (Amos 6:6): one said -- kenishkanin [many-spouted vessels]
and one said: that they throw their cups to one another
Rabba bar Rav Huna came to the Exilarch's house, and [the Exilarch] drank from kenishkanin
and [Rabba bar Rav Huna] said nothing at all to him
Abaye: whatever has pleasure and has joy -- the Rabbis decreed on it
Abaye: but whatever has pleasure and no joy -- the Rabbis did not decree on it

supports.gloss_en: הכי נמי דאסיר? והא רבה בר רב הונא איקלע לבי ריש גלותא ואישתי בקנישקנין ולא אמר ליה ולא מידי -- a pleasure the verse names was not forbidden (kind svara: no support kind names a ma'aseh)

objections.gloss_en: מתיב רב יוסף: אף על פלייטון גזר רבי יהודה בן בבא ולא הודו לו; ואי אמרת משום תענוג, אמאי לא הודו לו? -- if the verse condemns palyaton for its pleasure, why did the Sages reject the decree on it?

answered_by.gloss_en: ולטעמיך -- the same verse's mizrekei (kenishkanin) would then be forbidden too, yet Rabba bar Rav Huna said nothing when [the Exilarch] drank from them; אלא: the Rabbis decreed on pleasure with joy, not on pleasure without joy (= p_taanug_vesimcha_gazru, p_taanug_belo_simcha_lo_gazru)
